settings.acceptedTimingBasis: prepare-toccata.py retains the accepted score's quarterBpm 60 from prepare-opening.py, so its pinned mapping beats encode seconds

observation: Renderer iteration snapshots; runs group identical frequency/control observations, not score notes or bus writes
limitations: Times bracket observed states at the snapshot cadence. Mid-call partial frequency words, unobserved writes, effects and repeated same-pitch notes can affect runs. One-snapshot states are excluded by default. Matches compare pitch classes only; frequency effects may produce incidental nominal pitches. No hearing, exact gate, harmonic-equivalence or full-form claim follows.

acceptedSections.name: Octave triplets and descending broken intervals
acceptedSections.reduction: RH upper line on melody and LH lower octave on bass; keep the written octave dialogue without inventing a percussion part. The notated long rests are deliberately compressed.

acceptedSections.name: Second diminished hold and decorated arrival
acceptedSections.reduction: Reserve bass for the pedal, melody for the latest RH onset, and harmony for the lower remaining manual tone. Cycle selected source chord tones during the hold; omit remaining doublings. The printed F4 trill is realized independently of MIDI.

acceptedSections.name: Running right hand against repeated A accompaniment
acceptedSections.reduction: RH remains foreground even after descending below the offbeat LH A4. Put each LH A4 on the quieter harmony patch one octave lower; bass is reserved for written pedal notes.

acceptedSections.name: Interleaved hands and pedal replies
acceptedSections.reduction: The newest manual onset owns melody, regardless of pitch or hand; simultaneous dyads retain their lower tone on harmony when possible. Bass retains the pedal. Omit additional sustained or doubled tones rather than masking the moving line.

acceptedSections.name: Diminished pillar and paired triplet descent
acceptedSections.reduction: The held chord uses pedal plus lead and selected harmony cycling. At source beat 86 the tied C#5 and E4 become the first triplet notes, despite having begun at beat 84. Subsequent RH/LH triplets keep independent melody/bass lanes.

acceptedSections.name: Cadential chord replies and pedal run
acceptedSections.reduction: Retain the pedal run and each upper chord attack; a single harmony voice cycles source-backed interior tones only during the four longer chord replies. Upper octave doublings remain explicit omissions.

acceptedSections.name: Upper resolution with moving inner voice
acceptedSections.reduction: Keep F4 then E4 on melody, D4 then C#4 on harmony, and the written pedal. G3 replaces the last quarter-beat of the C#4 inner sustain at 115.75 to expose the final inner resolution; omit A3 doubling.

acceptedSections.name: Final D minor inner resolution and warm hold
acceptedSections.reduction: D4 melody and D2 pedal remain sustained while harmony exposes G3–F3–E3–F3. Omit the simultaneous D3/A3 doublings. The final F3 is a sustained minor third rather than an arpeggio; the authored three-second last-beat hold precedes release.
